result: SUPERSEDED: old generic SMHC0-2 descriptor/control assumptions withdrawn; do not deploy bound old package
reviewed: Card CMD_DONE and DATA_OVER/AUTO_COMMAND_DONE plus direction-specific IDST are required before success. All active descriptor OWN bits must clear; descriptor error fails the request.
Coherent allocations use a 32-bit DMA mask; descriptor/data/next addresses are word-shifted and checked for alignment/end bounds. The 1KiB chunks avoid ambiguous 11-bit zero encoding.
dma_wmb orders initialized descriptors and outgoing data before starting IDMA. dma_rmb precedes descriptor and incoming buffer consumption.
Every launched data request stops/disables/resets the DMA controller and FIFO before read-copy, successful return or memory reuse.
Any reset timeout sets dma_dead/ios_error; future commands refuse operation. Both coherent allocations remain pinned on remove and failure cleanup rather than being freed for a potentially late DMA.
Failed reads do not copy bounce contents to caller SG; bytes_xfered remains zero. Short SG copy fails before starting DMA on writes.
Ordered WQ serializes work and supports requeue from mmc_request_done. The running callback makes no further mrq access after completion.
SBC failure is returned; request errors attempt CMD12; dma_dead makes the stop command fail safely without re-enabling the engine.
DMA status error bits agree with Tina sunxi-mmc.h: fatal bus 2, destination-invalid 4, card-error 5, abnormal-summary 9, host-abort 10.
Last descriptor CHAIN+LAST+END, DIC cleared, next zero matches the existing mainline sunxi-mmc descriptor termination; Tina uses CHAIN+LAST and omits END. Both use LAST to terminate data.

Final t736_check_dma_bus only readl()s two resources; builder supplies exact corrected addresses 0x020025e0 and 0x0200259c. It requires STORE_MBUS bit30 and MSI_LITE1 bit0, returning before controller writes on failure. No new writes to either shared clock register.
Saved board snapshot at corrected addresses reads f1055803/00030001 and SMCV03050610. Prior wrong-address zero readings are superseded, not evidence that DMA bus gates were off.

Production polling calls t736_dma_poll_result from the same header compiled by the actual C tests. The extracted helper preserves error priority, CMD/data/directional DMA completion and dma_rmb-before-OWN semantics.

Reviewed new C test cases cover missing CMD/data/direction bits, auto-stop, pending intermediate OWN, descriptor error and simultaneous error/completion. Independent review did not repeat the build-owner test run.
retained_limitations: This review is not a DMA hardware test or higher-speed timing acceptance.
Two-second command/busy budget and existing auto-stop response handling are inherited from the v16 path.
Timing remains 12MHz legacy 8-bit; no high-speed/MMC voltage capability is enabled.
Quarantined memory is intentionally leaked until reboot after a dead DMA engine.
required_hardware_acceptance: Confirm SMHC version guard, low32-bit descriptor/data addresses and unchanged 12MHz legacy IOS.
Cold boot through rootfs, compare bounded raw-read checksums, bounded filesystem write/read checksums, and inspect controller errors.
Test request boundary/fragment sizes and preserve working kernel/DTB/PVR/initrd rollback.
excludes: No approval for later source changes or any new shared STORE_MBUS/MSI_LITE register writes
reviewed_revision: final DMA candidate with corrected CCU read-only checks and shared completion helper
superseded_reason: Manual Table11-4/11-6 and section11.3.9 define SMHC3-specific reserved bits; corrected candidate requires fresh hashes and review
latest_findings: Agree DES0 only OWN/FD/LD under low4G; CES30 is reserved, not error
Agree DMAC enables bit7 only, bit1 reserved
Agree IDST valid clear mask0x133 and errors4/5
Additional correction requested: RINTSTS13 is read start-error but write busy-clear; RINTSTS18 is data write busy timeout
